slides.visual_description: Module 1 Completion and Forward-Looking Close — Understand the closing summary that marks Module 1 complete and signals a transition from mindset to the learner's next stage.
slides.narration_text: Congratulations—Module 1 is complete. You’ve built the cognitive foundation: a way of seeing, diagnosing, and sensing opportunity inside the hospital. That matters because from this point, your mindset stops being an internal compass and starts becoming a leadership engine. Treat this as a handoff: from how you think to how you lead.
slides.script_notes: Module 1 Completion and Forward-Looking Close — Understand the closing summary that marks Module 1 complete and signals a transition from mindset to the learner's next stage.

slides.display_title: Bridge from Mindset to Leadership Identity
slides.visual_description: Bridge from Mindset to Leadership Identity — Understand that Module 2 shifts the learner from innovation mindset toward leadership identity inside the health system.
slides.narration_text: With the mindset set, let’s cross the bridge. On one side, where you’ve been is an innovation mindset—curiosity, questioning, and possibility. On the other side, where you’re going is leadership identity—owning your role, your voice, and your influence inside the health system. In Module 2 we’ll make that move explicitly, translating insight into identity so people can feel and follow your direction.
slides.script_notes: Bridge from Mindset to Leadership Identity — Understand that Module 2 shifts the learner from innovation mindset toward leadership identity inside the health system.

slides.visual_description: Module 1 Mindset Pillars Recap — Understand the core conceptual pillars that define the innovation mindset established in Module 1.
slides.narration_text: Before we step fully into identity, lock in the pillars that define the mindset you just built. These pillars shift you from reactive to generative leadership: diagnose first—see the real problem before reaching for solutions; sense opportunity—notice the white space others overlook; practice cross‑functional flexibility—move across silos and disciplines; create psychological safety—so bold ideas can surface; act as an enabler—your sponsorship determines whether opportunity moves; and finally, prize execution over ideas—impact lives through action, not ideation alone.
slides.script_notes: Module 1 Mindset Pillars Recap — Understand the core conceptual pillars that define the innovation mindset established in Module 1.

slides.visual_description: Diagnostic and Problem-Finding Pillars — Understand that innovation starts with diagnosing the real operational problem rather than prematurely committing to a solution.
slides.narration_text: Great innovators start by choosing the right problem. That means asking, “What is actually broken?” and pushing past presenting symptoms to surface root causes. It also means resisting premature closure—don’t anchor to the first plausible fix. And verify your diagnosis with frontline insight so the picture reflects lived operational reality. Slow down to speed up.
slides.script_notes: Diagnostic and Problem-Finding Pillars — Understand that innovation starts with diagnosing the real operational problem rather than prematurely committing to a solution.

slides.visual_description: Opportunity, Flexibility, and Safety Pillars — Understand that effective healthcare innovation also depends on opportunity sensing, cross-functional flexibility, and psychological safety.
slides.narration_text: Beyond diagnosis, innovation takes three reinforcing behaviors. First, opportunity sensing—train your attention to spot gaps in care, workflow friction, and unmet patient needs before they harden into crises. A separate thread is cross‑functional flexibility—build bridges across clinical, operational, and administrative lines so solutions can travel. A distinct angle is psychological safety—teams speak up and take smart risks only when leaders truly welcome candor.
slides.script_notes: Opportunity, Flexibility, and Safety Pillars — Understand that effective healthcare innovation also depends on opportunity sensing, cross-functional flexibility, and psychological safety.

slides.display_title: The Leader as the Constraint or Enabler
slides.visual_description: The Leader as the Constraint or Enabler — Understand that opportunities only become viable when a capable leader can champion them through the health system.
slides.narration_text: You’ve now got the pillars; the lever is you. In complex systems, opportunities live or die based on the champion. The same role can produce two outcomes: as a constraint, a leader avoids risk, hoards information, and reinforces hierarchy; as an enabler, a leader sponsors ideas, removes barriers, and builds coalition support. You are not neutral—your posture, priorities, and political capital either open or close the door.
slides.script_notes: The Leader as the Constraint or Enabler — Understand that opportunities only become viable when a capable leader can champion them through the health system.

slides.display_title: Why Ideas Alone Are Not Enough
slides.visual_description: Why Ideas Alone Are Not Enough — Understand that innovation success in a matrixed health system depends far more on leadership execution than on having a good idea alone.
slides.narration_text: Here’s the hard truth: ideas don’t fail because they’re unoriginal; they fail because execution stalls. Compared with a great idea under weak leadership—which sinks into committees, loses momentum, and never scales—a good idea under strong leadership navigates politics, builds alliances, and reaches system‑level adoption. Execution is the differentiator: innovation success is 20% idea quality and 80% leadership execution. The mindset you’ve built is necessary—but not sufficient on its own.
slides.script_notes: Why Ideas Alone Are Not Enough — Understand that innovation success in a matrixed health system depends far more on leadership execution than on having a good idea alone.

slides.visual_description: Leadership Capabilities to Build Next — Understand the specific leadership dimensions Module 2 will develop: identity, communication, and the ability to inspire others.
slides.narration_text: Now we develop the capabilities that turn mindset into movement. First, leadership identity—clarify who you are as a leader and what you stand for in the health system. Second, strategic communication—frame your ideas compellingly for diverse stakeholders and executive audiences. Third, inspiring others—motivate teams, build coalitions, and move people toward a shared vision. That’s the path into Module 2; the clinical problem is waiting, so let’s build the leader who will solve it.
slides.script_notes: Leadership Capabilities to Build Next — Understand the specific leadership dimensions Module 2 will develop: identity, communication, and the ability to inspire others.
